A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Absolute Zero Reasoner study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support comparison, with corresponding material identifiable despite pagination and figure-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original AZR training and evaluation results, including benchmark scores, scaling experiments, ablations, and appendix analyses and examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds pass@k evaluations and MMLU-Pro comparisons in Figures 8–9.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the three reasoning tasks, TRR++, and training hyperparameters are retained. However, Equation (3) moves lambda between reward terms, while Equation (6) replaces 'passable' with 'correctly formatted', overlapping its wrong-but-well-formatted case. The PDFs do not establish whether these specification edits intend a change in training behavior.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU-Pro evaluation across 14 subjects, including business, law, psychology, biology, and health. This substantially extends evaluated domains beyond the retained mathematics, coding, and appendix puzzle tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged. The new evaluations reuse existing comparators: Qwen2.5-7B for pass@k, and Qwen2.5-7B, ORZ-7B, and SimpleRL-Zoo-7B for MMLU-Pro; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: RQ8 adds a substantially different evaluation design: pass@k curves with temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, a 16k output limit, and k up to 512, alongside retained greedy evaluations. RQ9 adds MMLU-Pro evaluation with greedy decoding and a 16k limit. LiveCodeBench is relabeled from v5 to v1–5, May 2023–February 2025; unchanged scores do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: The new RQ8/Figure 8 analysis tests whether AZR preserves reasoning coverage as sampling budgets increase across five benchmarks, a diagnostic absent from v1. Existing task/proposer ablations, training-dynamics analyses, complexity/diversity measures, case studies, and alternative approaches remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark comparisons. The new pass@k sampling changes the evaluation design, without adding uncertainty estimates or replicated-training reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 add substantial new results: AZR-Base-7B leads the base model on four of five high-pass@k comparisons, with AIME24 at k=512 the exception, and achieves the highest MMLU-Pro subject and overall averages among the four compared models. Original Tables 1, 2, and 5 retain their numerical results, including AZR-Coder-7B's 50.4 overall average.

T1.justification: Equation (3) changes from proposer reward plus lambda-weighted solver reward to lambda-weighted proposer reward plus solver reward. Under the stated nonnegative lambda, this changes which objective remains at lambda=0. Equation (4)'s removal of the explicit success-rate-one branch is algebraically equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: self-proposed training without external curated data, leading combined coding/mathematics performance, cross-domain transfer, and applicability across model sizes and families. The additional evaluations support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 interprets high-pass@k results as preserved reasoning coverage and compatibility with test-time scaling, and MMLU-Pro results as evidence of broader generalization. It also replaces the suggestion that proposer training may be relatively noncritical with emphasis on improving it through interference mitigation and broader task coverage. Existing safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly states that each experiment takes approximately 3–5 days on the already disclosed A800 GPU clusters. v3 also supplies decoding parameters for its added evaluations. Training hyperparameters, executable examples, prompts, and code/model/log access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 expands references to autotelic agents and learning-progress research, including Colas, Haluptzok, Oudeyer, MAGELLAN, and ACES, and adds recent self-play and evaluation-related citations. The overall novelty positioning remains. DeepSeek-AI becoming Guo et al. represents an updated reference to the same work.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the abstract, preliminaries, method explanations, and proposer discussion, plus new RQ8–9 paragraphs and acknowledgements. The main section organization and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the five-panel pass@k plot and MMLU-Pro grouped bar chart as Figures 8–9. Existing displays are largely retained, with localized reflow, LiveCodeBench header/caption edits, and corresponding appendix figure renumbering rather than a visual overhaul.

improvement.justification: The added pass@k and MMLU-Pro evaluations strengthen empirical support for reasoning coverage and generalization beyond mathematics and coding. Runtime disclosure and additional relevant prior work also improve transparency. These are bounded gains focused on one 7B variant; uncertainty reporting remains absent, and v3 introduces reward-condition ambiguity and an incorrect figure reference in RQ8.
